newsitem.title: MEXICO: SOCCER-HERMOSILLO SCORES TWICE AS MEXICO HAMMER CANADA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HERMOSILLO SCORES TWICE AS MEXICO HAMMER CANADA.

text.p: Striker Carlos Hermosillo scored twice as Mexico began the final stage of the CONCACAF World Cup qualifiers with a 4-0 win over Canada on Sunday.
Mexico dominated the game in front of a 100,000 crowd but took until the 50th minute to find a way past goalkeeper Craig Forrest.
Luis Hernandez, who came on as a halftime substitute, made a superb run down the right and crossed for Hermosillo to break the deadlock with a header at the far post.
Benmajin Galindo increased Mexico's lead from the penalty spot nine minutes later after Lyndon Hooper used his hands to stop a shot by Brazilian-born striker Zague.

Hermosillo, who had been overlooked by the national team until this year despite a record as the country's most prolific goalscorer, scored again in the 80th minute when he finished off a move involving Hernandez and Ramon Ramirez.
Zague, jeered after wasting a good first half chance, blasted in the fourth goal three minutes from time.

The result may lift the pressure on coach Bora Milutinovic, under fire for some poor results in the previous stage of the qualifiers when Mexico, despite going through, lost away to Jamaica and Honduras.
The top three teams qualify from the six-team final stage group which also includes Jamaica, the United States, Costa Rica and El Salvador.
